暂无信息

On Scope, a user by the handle “McHarris” has been dropping evidence of a “No Man’s Nova” – an eerie parallel to our world, but devoid of life, causing a stir online. Despite the doubters, interactive checks have pretty much confirmed its existence.

McHarris insists it’s an exact replica of Nova, boasting regular day-night transitions, air circulation, and fully operational utilities. The only twist? It’s a ghost town for lifeforms, Chaos included. However, plants seem to flourish as usual.
It’s somehow entwined with our reality, sharing network signals. Through specific methods, goods can even be swapped between the two, but they appear reversed in the opposing realm.
This space’s origin and access method, and whether it holds more than just Nova City, remain shrouded in mystery. Some theorize it’s tied to people creating second identities online.
Sonic Boom pulsated with the sounds of Harvey, the controversial heavy metal icon.
His magnetic musical prowess clashed with his anti-Chaos and Channeler lyrics, drawing a largely fanatical, biased crowd with a deep disdain for both.
Their frenzied energy birthed a sudden surge of Chaos energy, transforming attendees into hybrid Chaos-human forms. Even Harvey wasn’t spared.
Ironically, the fear and animosity toward Chaos inadvertently birthed it, a twisted manifestation of Murphy’s Law with a darkly comedic edge…

As for why Harvey is so hostile towards Chaos? He’s never given a straight answer, but whispers in the streets suggest his lyrics reflect the infamous “Anti-Chaos Broadcasts,” painting him as a paranoid, indoctrinated conspiracy theorist—a notion gaining traction within select circles.

Rogue high beam use remains a significant headache for traffic departments worldwide. According to last year’s NCCA report, Nova grappled with 10,262 traffic incidents, 6,160 of which occurred at night, resulting in 1,121 casualties. A staggering 34.5% of these nighttime accidents were linked to high-beam use.
The “Nyx Veil,” a Chaos entity born from these tragic events,

Is believed to materialize from the fragmented will of the victims. Typically concealed, it requires specific stimuli to manifest. When visible, its pitch-black form lacks distinct features, save for a humanoid silhouette.

Its presence gives rise to the “Shadow Domain,” a dark zone of 10 to 100 meters, which absorbs 90% of light, disrupting all light sources and engulfing the area in profound darkness. While this darkness doesn’t directly inflict harm, the compromised visibility poses significant risks.
The entity’s behavior varies with the will of the deceased. Even those appearing benign are unpredictable and should be treated as hazardous.
The ACD urges all citizens to recognize that the “Nyx Veil” are perilous Chaos entities, regardless of their resemblance to loved ones.

Recently, pixelated projections of classic movie scenes have been popping up around Nova. The images bear a striking resemblance to the long-lost Strellares father and daughter who vanished over a decade ago, hinting at their potential creation of these projections from within the cinematic realm.
The projections lack physical form but can emit sound via snippets of movie dialogue. Devoid of Chaos energy, they’ve been deemed harmless, evolving into a popular tourist attraction in Nova.
Their pixelated appearance likely stems from variances in the laws of physics between the cinematic realm and reality, rather than any intentional design.
In Nova, there’s an old urban legend about a magical movie ticket that lets you jump into movie worlds and switch between them and the real world.

The earliest known account of this legend dates back to the disappearance of the Strellares father-daughter duo from over a decade ago. They simply vanished within a movie theater, and signs point to their immersion into the cinematic realm, where they’ve likely been dwelling since.
Lately, numerous pixelated projections of iconic movie scenes have surfaced, believed to be the handiwork of the missing duo, sparking a craze in Nova.

Research shows that the cinematic realm’s laws of physics vastly diverge from our reality, particularly concerning time. Here, past and future blend seamlessly; time is exceedingly flexible and nonlinear, caught in a perpetual loop, out of sync with real-world time.
There exists only one “Legit Movie Ticket” to the cinematic realm. However, owing to temporal disparities between the two realms, multiple individuals may possess it simultaneously in the real world.

In the dynamic urban sprawl, an assortment of carbonated beverages has seamlessly melded into the tapestry of modern existence. Notably, Tuto Foods’ Original Rabbit Cola has emerged as a quintessential favorite. However, this popular soda has led to a group of people who drink Rabbit Cola daily, giving rise to the high-risk Chaos known as “Infinite Rabbit Cola.”

Whenever this Rift occurs, surrounding natural water bodies undergo an abrupt transformation, turning into Rabbit Cola. Besides housing Chaos energy, this Cola mirrors the exact composition of Tuto Foods’ Original Rabbit Cola. Although harmless, “Infinite Rabbit Cola” can gradually turn other water bodies into Cola, potentially causing massive natural disasters.

If it were to infiltrate atmospheric rain clouds, leading to a global downpour of Cola, the ecosystem could face obliteration within moments. The high calorie and sugar content of the Cola could swiftly decimate all plant life. The subsequent release of CO2 would induce a greenhouse effect, melting glaciers, flooding continents, and destroying human civilization.
Hence, the renowned Chaos explorer, Bear Grayson, issues a poignant reminder: Water is the wellspring of existence, not soda.
Human’s relentless pursuit of efficiency led to the birth of this Chaos, causing the signal towers themselves to chaosify. This Chaos can boost signal efficiency based on a human’s desire.
However, human desires are infinite, which ultimately led to the signal towers overloading, resulting in a total communications breakdown.
For unknown reasons, a series of self-replicating micro robots went haywire and scurried across the city, developing a sense of self-awareness.
They autonomously hack into signal towers, sending strange messages to the phones of people nearby.

A Chaos mutated from humans, believed to have originated from an arcade running game called “Turbo Rampager.” Players experience vivid running hallucinations and then start sprinting in real life with extraordinary stamina.

Upon complete transformation into “Turbo Rampagers,” players lose consciousness and become speed-driven entities, running until their life force is drained. A motorcycle-like appendage emerges from their head, their skull reshaping into a tire while handlebar grips extend outward.
This mutation is irreversible. Records show a victim ran for a month until their body reached its limit and disintegrated into dust.
Another theory posits that the root cause of Turbo Rampager lies in the overwhelming, unrelenting stress of modern life, with the game serving as a mere trigger, not the cause.

Created by fanatics under the sway of the “Anti-Chaos Forum,” these gadgets pack a battery, digital transmitter, and speaker. They keep spewing out wild theories from the forum for a solid 72 hours, using digital signals and sound waves.

But watch out—infused with Chaos energy, these signals and waves can seriously mess with your head. If you try to smash it, be ready for a Chaos energy explosion. It’s best to disable it before dismantling.
Despite their diverse appearances, all Anti-Chaos Broadcast share a suspiciously similar build. Makers insist they were “inspired” to create them, hinting at a possible collective Chaos manipulation.
Further investigations are ongoing.

Under the cover of night on the streets of Nova, burdened souls might catch sight of a gentle, radiant beam of light. Should they be driven by curiosity and draw near, they will encounter three shadows resembling themself. These figures, claiming to represent the person’s Original Self, Present Self, and Aspirational Self, respond with cryptic, thought-provoking wisdom.

Some report the trio leads them on a nocturnal race through Nova’s streets. But instead of fatigue, they experience a sense of inner calm. After the race, the shadows bid a tranquil farewell, and the individual finds themselves back in Nova. All report feeling recharged and “living life to the max” afterward.
Interestingly, while the individuals note they are still in Nova during the race, they don’t see anyone else on the streets.
Some theorize that the Light of Heart triggers a mental illusion, conjuring the sensation of a midnight escapade.
Lately, this funky Chaos energy haze has been hovering over MM, stirring up worry among Nova locals about their well-being.
The rumor mill’s churning out wild guesses on how it materialized, giving birth to some whack conspiracy theories.
Truth is, the haze is just a byproduct of Pinchbot using stolen air purifiers during their “Grill and Chill” party, which inadvertently purified the Chaos energy.

Originally imported by Healing Star Pharma from Blissland, these eye drops were meant to soothe tired eyes. However, the Blissland manufacturer soon issued a recall due to potential vision issues. Healing Star Pharma then immediately halted sales. Leftover batches started surfacing in the Chaos underground market.
The ACD discovered this Chaos elixir messes with the optic nerve, letting users see the unseen and even distort perceptions based on their resistance.
This Mimic Chaos, a variant of the Pinchbot, takes the form of a cement mixer and can eject sand and gravel from its top.
Imported to Nova for construction purposes, these Chaos can enhance each other’s capabilities when gathered in large numbers, creating vast areas of turbulent sandstorms.

Invisible to the naked eye, these enigmatic Chaos, dubbed String Puppets, bear an eerie resemblance to the upper half of a human body, sporting unnervingly oversized hands in place of a head, clasping an eyeball-like crystal.
They latch onto people by sending out “threads” and suck out their desires.

Current research shows that these Chaos originate from “nightmares.” Initial symptoms include intense fatigue and mental depletion, accompanied by a waning interest in all activities. After 7 days, the victim becomes a complete empty shell.
Robert, a free climber without any Psionic Power, gained fame for ascending over seventy skyscrapers across the globe. Almost every towering structure in the city bears his footprints.

Fueled by the awe of onlookers, Robert’s Chaos Shadow scales the walls of skyscrapers. Despite numerous attempts, innumerable falls, and perilous gambles, he persistently targets the top. That’s the human drive to dominate.
Early this century, a new “Iron Tree” Chaos, stemming from the heart of urban sprawls, began to manifest after nightfall.

The Signal Tree, composed of traffic lights and metal poles, pulsates with red, green, and amber lights. Operating akin to real-world traffic lights, this Chaos abides by similar rules: move only on green. Move on red and you’ll be instantly ejected.
Fun Fact: When Signal Trees were first introduced a century ago, they played a pivotal role in emphasizing the importance of rule compliance.
Strange floating letters aglow with a subtle radiance, making it difficult for the naked eye to detect any anomalies.
The contents of the letter will continue to change until it gets close to any “recipient,” at which point it will begin to solidify.
The texts are mostly warnings for the “recipient,” and according to records of the contained Unstable Letter, these warnings always come true shortly after.

Formerly part of the Televised Collective, Sivalor has since become a certified member of the ACD, thriving in the underbelly of the city. He calls a trash can home and makes a living through divination.
Known for his knack of taming Chaos, Sivalor brought a Greedy Pinchbot under his sway after coming to Nova City, dubbing it Yellow Dog.
During his ACD registration test, Sivalor displayed Yellow Dog’s talent by having it fetch a bone for the Agents.
These canine‑esque graffiti Chaos once protected the residents of Paradox Plaza in rougher times.
Gentle by nature, they developed complex emotions from living alongside humans, and they always include their name when they speak; perhaps out of fear of forgetting who they are?
Over time, Paradox Plaza became less chaotic and people no longer needed them. These changes have washed much of their color away and left them considerably smaller.

A batch of chaos-imbued metal found its way into the car production line, causing vehicles manufactured during that time to chaosify and gain transformation abilities. These cars were shipped worldwide from MM Trade Port.
While most operated as regular vehicles without displaying hostile tendencies,

a handful absorbed language from radio broadcasts and begun communicating through iconic movie lines. Leveraging their sturdy metal frames, they menaced, coerced, and played pranks on unsuspecting individuals.
In response, MM tasked the ACD with orchestrating a comprehensive worldwide recall to rein in these renegade automobiles.
Tucked away in Row 12, Zone 3 North, MM, Portview Lane, lies Factory G19. Inside, a trove of antiquated communication devices, diodes, and triodes pepper the space.

This space exhibits composite Rifts. Amidst the labyrinth of equipment, a symphony of crackling transmissions echo through the air, hinting at magnetic disturbances. Standing as a monolithic enigma, the industrial marvel “Coeus” appears in this space, operating without any discernible power source.
Investigations attribute the composite Rifts within this space to the influence of the Chaos “Radionaut.” Consequently, no extraordinary measures are considered necessary for this peculiar anomaly.

Nestled in the heart of Downtown South at 12-4 Road, this iconic building has been a mainstay for over four decades. Within its halls, the Chaos entity known as “Flying Whalebone” occupies a place of reverence—an immense whale fall named Gary, unearthed a decade earlier in a neighboring basin by the Nova Oceanic Institute.

Once the institute completed researching it, they donated the whale skeleton to then under-construction library. This colossal skeleton symbolizes the often overlooked yet indispensable support within Nova’s intricate fishery ecosystem.

Since the library’s inauguration, Gary has silently borne witness to the fervent pursuits of students and scientists, even viewing the transformation of Lykaia from a young officer to Nova’s Prime Minister.

Over time, visitors have come to regard Gary as the symbolic curator, finding solace in the presence of the colossal creature. As Gary’s influence subtly permeated the collective subconscious, the once dormant tail began to stir once more. Now, as the vigilant guardian of the Whalebone Library, Gary safeguards knowledge seekers while keeping troublemakers in check, ensuring that those who respect its sanctity are granted unhindered access to its wealth of wisdom.

Situated within the bustling confines of West Glimmergold at 2-23, this independent art gallery once stood as a bastion of creative expression, presided over by the enigmatic curator, Myatt Blackburn.

Once a hub for grand exhibitions, the gallery’s illustrious past was marred by tragedy. Two decades ago, a devastating fire claimed several lives, including that of the curator’s daughter, igniting a maelstrom of controversy. Subsequently sealed off, the gallery lay dormant.

This space showed signs of chaosfication ten days ago, causing a swarm of Glimmergold locals to uncontrollably visit the gallery. But things took a nasty turn five days ago when curator Myatt Blackburn began showing signs of being “Eclipsed,” triggering the emergence of a “Brutal” Chaos Space right in the gallery. From within, numerous azure, human-like limbs burst out of the paintings, almost pulsating with life. A viscous, paint-like substance oozed from the artworks, inflicting grievous burns upon contact. Those ensnared within the Chaos Space assimilated into the very fabric of the paintings, consumed by the haunting appendages. The chaosfied space has since been neutralized by purifying the Eclipsed target.
A mysterious Chaos entity dwelling within the labyrinthine sewage system of Nova, boasting a jelly-like form.
Shy yet inquisitive, they frequently peer through manholes, startling passersby and causing accidents.
A bunch of dudes vibing on 80s radio rock, with an obsessive love for music, ended up creating these noisy Chaos by constantly setting up private radio stations.

Tune into 1130 AM and it’s like the ghost of the legendary late-night radio host Jonathan Logan is back, with his unique throat clearing and all. But there’s more: 80.0 FM sounds like a world-weary woman, 81.3 FM sounds like a little kid, and there’s even a wise elder in the mix.

They’re dubbed “Radionauts” by the young crowd, and it fits. These rebels hack into mainstream pop channels, swapping them for their own shows. Not everyone’s feeling their vibe, though—ACD is constantly flooded with complaints about them.
While dodging ACD Agents, they ran into a girl at MM. who said, “You know, your voices are kinda dope. ”
Paradox Plaza’s iconic buildings were erected by homeless folks over a decade ago. Two towers stand tall:
One a tribute to the fighters who battled for their homes, a symbol of freedom; the other a reminder of lessons learned from reckless actions, both stirring up painful memories.

When building the second Haunted High-Rise, a “videotape” got stashed in a shipping container. Soon, the container “fortress” around the Haunted High-Rise turned into Chaos because of the “videotape,” forming a crazy maze. The “videotape” got buried in the old treasures of Paradox. It wasn’t until the Paradox Championships started that it popped back into the public eye.
Common doves of Nova City, enlarged by Chaos. These once serene birds have transformed into notorious snack snatchers, targeting the bustling office lunch crowd.
A humanoid Chaos, composed of three elusive entities concealed beneath a billowing trench coat. It replicates human movements but remains devoid of speech.
Concealed within corner crevices, these mysterious Chaos entities reach out with shadowy hands to rend gaps in walls, their radiant eyes fixated on all who pass by.
Nova’s late-night coastal boulevard is a bustling hotspot for strollers, where the sea breeze intensifies emotions.
This collective energy spawns Chaos, causing the streetlights to come to life and wander aimlessly about.
Come dawn, they often struggle to find their way back without assistance.

Atop certain buildings amidst the urban sprawl of Nova exist these concealed rifts, discernible solely to the perceptive eyes of qualified ACD Agents. These rifts appear as an array of doors in assorted shapes and are watched over by vigilant ACD Recording Crows.
Engage the crow to verify your ID and traverse the sequence of doors using the passcode it provides to unlock the elusive ACD Special Supply.

These supplies are as unpredictable as blind boxes, so brace yourself for anything from an anti-tank missile launcher to a stash of Rabbit Cola. Legend tells of an Agent who once stumbled upon a chest laden with Golvent Coins.
Word is, a few Nova ATMs have chaosified for who knows why. Post-transaction, users get hit with wild “service fees,” from bling to basic goods, totally random, no rhyme or reason.
Refuse the service fee and the ATM will chomp down on you.
Some say this Chaos sprung up with the mobile pay wave, as cash and cards took a hit, messing with ATM action.
A member of Buddy Paws, it shares its mother’s vocal tic and often tacks its own name onto what it says. It can turn Doodlebuns into members of its own kind.
Right now it’s trying to grow the family’s ranks. Everything it does is motivated purely by the desire to make sure people don’t forget their mother.
The Socket Mages are obsessed with spatial teleportation. They use the power grid and microwave for their “summoning ritual,” pulling objects from Chaos space or reality into the microwave.
If they manage to pull it off, it could revolutionize technology. If you spot a Socket Mage performing a ritual, lend a hand. You’ll be contributing to Chaos research.

Like humans, Nova’s Pinchbots have their own “tastes” and only dig certain types of waste. Sort your trash right, and they’ll be your street-cleaning sidekicks. But if you mess up, a showdown is bound to happen… and it won’t be pretty. Keep it clean, folks!
Same four legs, same straight spine. Human imagination turned ordinary signboards into “wild horses” longing for freedom.
Initially embraced as a fashionable Chaos, however, their V-shaped design made riding them a challenge. As their popularity waned, they transitioned into mobile ads.

Seeking a change of scenery from their daily store perches, some began wandering the streets, leading to numerous traffic issues. To evade capture, they occasionally freeze, blending in as regular signs.
Emerging from ACD, the Safety Sentinels, once blank signboards, were designed to govern Chaos energy, akin to the Visual Observer.
By utilizing safety signs as hosts, these Chaos beings embraced a tranquil demeanor, seamlessly integrating into the bustling cityscape.

Crafted from recycled paper, the Paper Crane mimics the behavior of pigeons and possesses a natural affinity for Chaos. Despite being unable to breed, they embark on extensive migrations during specific seasons.

Fun fact:
They use cardboard boxes as their nests in cities.
Born from people’s nostalgia for fireflies, these Chaos look like light bulbs with wings and live just a few days.
They bring light to spaces in need until their radiance fades. Once their lights go out, they transform into relics, repurposed by people as decorations.
“I feel invisible,” a poignant phrase turned reality. For those grappling with despair, a new problem has arises—Invisible Affliction.
Their very beings slowly fade, until they disappear entirely. ACD mandates these individuals to don attire, asserting that only continued perception can prevent their complete dissipation.
Based on the MM-06 vending machine and engineered to harness the city’s Chaos energy.

Enigmatic beings, yearning for escape or solace, converged at the vending machine. Their emotional turbulence spurred the collected Chaos energy to mimic their behavior, speech, and even memories, displaying emotions on the screen.
Invisible to the naked eye, the Reflected Dove can only be seen via specialized optical lenses attuned to Rift detection.
A bunch of these Chaos critters have been found around Nova, prompting the installation of high-tech surveillance gear.
A Chaos variety found possessing traffic lights, not to be confused with the Signal Tree. The “Traffic Light Watcher” simply makes the lights move around as if they were eyeballs.
Due to its ability to reduce traffic accidents, the authorities have given it the green light to exist.

Fun fact:
It doesn’t have any special effects, merely catches people’s attention with its rotating eyeballs.

Integral to the Nova Rail Transit team, handling ticketing and maintenance operations. Operating from hidden spaces behind the Chaosfied ticket machines, they meticulously monitor and maintain the system.
According to them, they come from an endless train.
They seek no reward, simply stating, “We just don’t want people boarding anymore.”
These peculiar Chaos stones sway in response to positive vibes.

Positioned strategically in the corners of parks and shopping lanes, they appear to deter menacing Chaos. However, when faced with super-powerful Chaos, they immediately flee or curl up in a corner, pretending to be ordinary stones.
The “Kitty Plushie” series features Chaos with certain biological traits. Perfect for people who want pets without the hassle—unless even tossing them into the washing machine is too much trouble.
These widely sought-after Chaos companions are available from “Kitty Plushie” claw machines. While naturally friendly, they maintain a wary disposition around other Chaos.
In rare cases, Jello Chaos inhabit empty dolls, preferring spacious plushies.
They uphold the head with their bell and manipulate the limbs using their tentacles.

Should curious bystanders peek inside, they might at first glimpse “absolute nothingness,” an enough eerie spectacle. Yet, they will swiftly discern a Jello Chaos coiled within, endeavoring to abscond with it.
An enigmatic pool of Chaos, often formed from Jello Chaos secretions. These pools usually emerge after rainfall, whisking away any being that ventures into them to uncharted destinations.
Stroll through the serene alleys of Nova after dark and you might chance upon such a statue that materializes out of nowhere.
Legend has it that lingering thoughts are ensnared within these statues, incapable of liberation unless you avert your gaze from their piercing stare.
With cameras for heads, these crows surveil the city for the ACD, keeping tabs on Chaos and Agents with equal interest in both.

The Morphing Raccoon, a Chaos entity, emerged from Nova’s “Bake-danuki” folklore. They possess the extraordinary ability to change forms or attach to humans. These enigmatic beings first emerged when Nova was just a fishing port, delighting in human interactions and leaving an enduring mark on the city’s now elderly.

With its natural habitat lost, sightings of this elusive entity have become increasingly scarce. Studies indicate they have concealed themselves within the city, entering a state of hibernation. There are whispers that they may even have transformed and assimilated into human society.

Studies suggest that they have concealed themselves within the city, entering a state of hibernation. Speculation abounds that they may even have transformed and assimilated into human society. The ACD hopes to investigate and regulate these Chaos entities to delve deeper into the world of folklore-based Chaos.
Once symbols of hope for children’s health and growth, the carp-shaped streamers have transformed into Chaos thanks to human determination and positivity.
As summer arrives, they roam through the city, springing from bodies of water.
However, the presence of towering skyscrapers leads to frequent collisions among these free-flying streamers. Helping them return to the sky seems to bring blessings.

日期： 3月4日 #r天气： 阴雨#r局里的下水道又堵了，后勤大爷神神秘秘拉着我说里面肯定有怪东西。我打着手电趴在水池边掏了半天，指尖突然碰到一坨冰凉凉的玩意儿，比果冻还滑弹。没等我捏两下搞清楚是什么，那东西“哧溜”一下顺着水流钻进暗管没影了。#r我敢打赌那是只水坊主。这帮胆小鬼最近越来越喜欢往局里跑，估计是知道我们这儿管饭。我故意假装收拾东西走了，躲在门后偷瞄，没一会儿就看见水池里探出个透明的半流体小脑袋，正探头探脑地研究我落下的扳手……行吧，你爱躲着看就看，只要别再把下水道堵死，随便你逛。

A Chaos resembling a pufferfish that usually lives in the water. When struck, it inflates and becomes exceptionally buoyant. If you tie enough angry Balloonfish to yourself, you could achieve an easy lift off. In this state, if it gets hit again, the Balloonfish will break free from the ropes and float away in a huff.
Due to their cute appearance, Rixxy Wonderland theme park has hired some of them as staff.
A Chaos from foreign lands. Unlike the dashing characters of nobility seen in films, this particular lord is anything but handsome, retaining instead a very primitive and terrifying appearance.

Because he can never quite fit in, he faces constant setbacks in life. Not only has his appearance become increasingly disheveled, but his abilities have also plummeted; now his fangs are only slightly more dangerous to humans than those of a feral cat. He usually finds solace in sneaking sips of coconut juice from supermarkets.

A water jug-shaped Chaos that drifts through the low skies of Nova City in search of barren soil to water in an attempt to bring buried seeds to life. Because of this trait, agricultural organizations have started to use them for production.
However, they sometimes mistakes human heads for land, and it will keep watering them until the “seeds” break through the surface.
The former mascot of Rodriguez Restaurant. Along with top-tier viral marketing, its flashy and quirky appearance once made the queues at Rodriguez the longest in the biz.

Amidst overwhelming promotion, a real Chaos gradually emerged. They resemble hot dogs and waddle down the streets of Nova City, aiming to make every inch of the city smell of their hot doggy goodness.

A humanoid piece of equipment originally developed by the ACD for exploring the Chaos Space. Arms nearly got destroyed during a mission and underwent Chaosification. He used parts from his own kind to repair himself.
As of the time of this recording, Arms has left the ACD and is now running Solution Pawn. Avoid buying any of the merchandise there, as it could lead to getting scammed.
